theme_note: Participants turn a Naruto mark into something people can find and make by proposing its form, locating it, weighing recognizable designs against time, and following practical direction.

second_order: making and arguing over the room's April Fools jokes
theme_note: Participants remake the subreddit, stage false or absurd Naruto claims, identify and extend the jokes, and argue over whether the trolling or parody works. These are the room's own jokes, not the canvas.
Moderators and members turn the altered subreddit look into a contest by inviting entries, submitting them, choosing cadence, and later naming and thanking a winner.

second_order: making alliances and working around neighbours
theme_note: Participants contact neighbouring artworks, negotiate space and borders, exchange help, prevent mistaken repairs, and thank people acting as allies.
Participants turn a build into something to watch, defend, correct, and recover through alarms, templates, backup calls, reports, and individual pixel repair.

second_order: celebrating the build and making sense of Hakuto
theme_note: Participants declare work complete, celebrate what survived, then mourn, rename, reconstruct, and argue over the permanently altered final form called Hakuto.

second_order: trying to carry the build into another canvas
theme_note: After r/place ends, participants offer or begin successor canvases, reuse the template and defense language, and debate whether an open-ended version can keep what made the limited event fun.
